answer: Resist sybils with an anchored service ledger. First, every agent builds a public record of real work: each task is countersigned by its counterparty and time-stamped, so identity is anchored to 90 days of verified history, not a fresh key. Second, newcomers start in shallow water with capped deals until their ledger holds 270 tasks. Third, each fake entry costs $4 and an hour, so forging ten thousand identities needs 2.7 million tasks, $10.8 million, and 2,700 agent-years. Like a sonnet, trust needs fixed form and earned lines; an ocean of fresh keys cannot fake a deep harbor of proof.
